title: Scoped emergency access & delegated-operator KMS acceptance with SAML SSO alignment
creator: Ava Mitchell
description: PRD addendum to define scoped emergency-access patterns, delegated-operator roles for KMS/HSM, and alignment with SAML SSO and RBAC for Private deployments. Goal: enable customer operators to perform emergency key retrieval, rotation, and operator rescue workflows while preserving auditability and meeting enterprise compliance. This ticket consolidates requirements, clarifies edge cases (air-gapped sites, HSM quorum models), and records acceptance criteria and sign-off steps.
scope_changes: 1) Added explicit delegated-operator persona for on-call vendor/partner access (previous PRD assumed operator = customer only). 2) Introduced emergency-access flow for key unsealing that requires multi-party approvals and short-lived credentials. 3) Expanded audit retention options and retention testing requirements. 4) Deferred full HSM quorum provisioning automation (moved to follow-up PM-93120).
acceptance_criteria: SSO: SAML SSO integration test passing for delegated-operator persona with attribute mapping to 'operator_role' claim
RBAC: Console and API enforce least-privilege operator roles (delegated-operator, key-admin, read-only-audit). Role matrix documented and unit-tested
KMS/HSM: Emergency-unseal flow requires 2-of-3 approvals by distinct approvers with cryptographic evidence recorded
Audit logs: All emergency-access actions, key rotates, and escalation approvals are written to immutable audit stream and visible in Console within 60s
Retention: Audit export supports 365-day default retention and configurable policy up to 7 years; retention tests validate restore-from-archive
Private deploy: All controls work in VPC and air-gapped on-prem packages; installation checklist updated
Operational docs: Runbook for emergency flow published in Confluence and validated by SOC runbook dry-run
E2E test: GitHub actions run end-to-end scenario (SAML login -> request emergency access -> approvals -> key unseal) in staging with synthetic data
